title: Crispy Masala Dosa with Coconut and Onion-Tomato Chutney
description: Crisp fermented rice-and-lentil dosas filled with a lightly spiced potato masala and served with coconut chutney and a tangy onion-tomato chutney.

ingredients.item: idli rice or sona masoori rice

ingredients.note: helps produce a golden, crisp dosa
for soaking, grinding, and adjusting the batter
thinly sliced; for the potato masala
adjust for the desired chutney consistency
roughly chopped; for the onion-tomato chutney

steps: Rinse the rice thoroughly and soak it with the fenugreek seeds for 4–6 hours.
Rinse the urad dal and chana dal, then soak them separately for 4–6 hours. Soak the poha for approximately 20 minutes before grinding.
Drain the urad dal mixture and grind it with cold water added gradually until the batter becomes very smooth, light, and fluffy.
Drain the rice and grind it with the soaked poha into a smooth but slightly grainy batter. Avoid adding excessive water.
Combine both batters in a large vessel and mix vigorously by hand for 2–3 minutes. The batter should be thick but pourable.
Cover loosely and ferment in a warm place for 8–12 hours, or until the batter has risen noticeably and smells mildly sour.
After fermentation, gently mix in the salt. Add a little water as required; the batter should spread easily without becoming watery.
For the potato masala, heat the oil and add the mustard seeds. Once they crackle, add the urad dal, chana dal, curry leaves, asafoetida, green chilies, and ginger.
Add the sliced onions and a pinch of salt. Cook until the onions soften but do not become deeply browned.
Add the turmeric, boiled potatoes, and water. Break the potatoes into uneven pieces while mixing and cook until the masala is moist but not watery.
Turn off the heat and finish the potato masala with cilantro and lemon juice. Keep it warm.
For the coconut chutney, blend the coconut, roasted chana dal, green chilies, ginger, salt, and water until smooth.
Heat the oil for the coconut chutney tempering. Add mustard seeds, urad dal, dried red chili, and curry leaves. Pour the tempering over the chutney.
For the onion-tomato chutney, heat the oil and roast the chana dal, urad dal, and dried red chilies until aromatic and lightly golden.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until softened. Add the tomatoes, tamarind, and salt, then cook until the tomatoes collapse and excess moisture evaporates.
Cool the onion-tomato mixture slightly and blend it into a smooth or slightly coarse chutney. Add a small amount of water only if necessary.
Heat a cast-iron or non-stick dosa tawa over medium-high heat. Sprinkle a few drops of water on it; they should evaporate immediately.
Lightly grease the tawa and wipe away the excess. Pour one ladle of batter in the center and spread it rapidly outward in concentric circles.
Drizzle oil, ghee, or butter around the edge and over the surface. Cook until the dosa becomes golden, crisp, and releases easily from the pan.
Place a portion of potato masala in the center, spread it slightly, and fold or roll the dosa.
Serve immediately with coconut chutney and onion-tomato chutney.
notes: Fermentation time depends heavily on room temperature. In a cold climate, place the batter in an oven with only the light switched on.
Do not use excess water while grinding. A thin batter ferments poorly and produces soft dosas.
The tawa must be hot enough to prevent sticking but not so hot that the batter sets before it can be spread.
Cool an overheated tawa by wiping it with a damp cloth or a cut onion before making the next dosa.
Salt the full batter only after fermentation unless your kitchen is very warm and fermentation is rapid.
Use oil instead of ghee or butter for a vegan version.
